text: I don't want to take away from the romanticism of it, it's just that it's most often we hear those romantic stories from the successes.
speaker: Andrew 'Boz' Bosworth
context: Lenny asks Boz about the early days at Facebook, noting that movies like The Social Network make starting a company look fun and glamorous. Boz explains that while those early startup days created great memories and camaraderie, they were forged through intense hardship - working 120 hours per week, gaining weight, having no social life, and constantly dealing with technical crises. He emphasizes that people only hear these romantic startup stories from the companies that succeeded, not from those who made similar sacrifices but didn't achieve success.
text_ko: 그 낭만적인 면을 깎아내리려는 건 아니에요. 다만 그런 낭만적인 이야기는 보통 성공한 사람들 얘기에서만 듣게 되는 경우가 많아요.
text_zh: 我不是想破坏这种浪漫色彩，只是这些励志故事往往都是成功者讲出来的。
text_es: No quiero quitarle lo romántico que tiene, pero la cosa es que casi siempre escuchamos esas historias románticas de los que ya la pegaron.
key_sentence: it's just that it's most often we hear those romantic stories from the successes.
original_text: I don't want to take away from the romanticism of it, it's just that it's most often we hear those romantic stories from the successes. It's a healthy thing for people to want to throw themselves into something and take that risk, but it is not glamorous at the time.

vocabulary.definition: Romanticism refers to a movement or perspective that emphasizes emotion, individualism, and the glorification of the past, particularly in art and literature.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, romanticism can manifest in the idealized narratives surrounding entrepreneurship, where the challenges and realities of starting a business are often overshadowed by success stories.
vocabulary.nuance: While romanticism can inspire and motivate, it may also lead to unrealistic expectations about the entrepreneurial journey.

vocabulary.definition: Successes are achievements or favorable outcomes that result from efforts, often measured against specific goals or benchmarks.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the context of business and startups, successes are often highlighted to attract investors, motivate teams, and build brand reputation.
vocabulary.nuance: While celebrating successes is important, it is equally crucial to acknowledge failures to provide a balanced view of the business landscape.

text: Your job is not to do it yourself. Your job is to get it done, is to have the thing done, done well, done right, done competently.
speaker: Andrew 'Boz' Bosworth
context: Lenny discusses Boz's popular advice about leveraging leaders more effectively. Boz explains that people often want to prove they can solve problems independently, but this misses the point of their actual job responsibilities. He argues that the goal isn't to demonstrate personal capability by working alone, but to achieve the best possible outcomes using all available resources - including the expertise, connections, and authority that managers and mentors possess.
text_ko: 당신의 일은 직접 처리하는 게 아니에요. 당신의 역할은 일이 끝나도록 만드는 거예요. 잘, 정확하게, 능숙하게 마무리되도록 하는 거예요.
text_zh: 你的工作不是亲力亲为，而是要把事情搞定，要做好、做对、做到位。
text_es: Tu trabajo no es hacerlo todo tú mismo. Tu trabajo es lograr que se haga, que las cosas salgan bien, que se hagan como debe ser, con profesionalismo.
key_sentence: Your job is to have the thing done competently, not to do it yourself.
original_text: Your job is not to do it yourself. Your job is to get it done, is to have the thing done, done well, done right, done competently. And a lot of times, the tools that you need to do that live with your manager, with your partner, with your advisor, with your mentor.

vocabulary.definition: In a manner that demonstrates the necessary skills and knowledge to perform a task effectively.
vocabulary.businessContext: Competence is crucial in the workplace, as it reflects an employee's ability to meet job expectations and contribute to team goals.
vocabulary.nuance: The term suggests a baseline level of proficiency; however, it may not imply excellence or exceptional performance.

text: Nobody wants you to be more awesome than your manager does, because when you're amazing, your manager, his life gets easier, her life gets easier. So, I just think that's the mentality we get into is like, 'No, no, no. They're testing me.' They're not.
speaker: Andrew 'Boz' Bosworth
context: Boz continues explaining why people should ask their managers for help more often. He uses an analogy from actor Patrick Stewart about auditions - casting directors want actors to succeed because it makes their job easier once they find the right person. Similarly, Boz argues that managers genuinely want their employees to excel because employee success directly makes the manager's work easier and more effective.
text_ko: 상사만큼 당신이 잘되길 바라는 사람은 없어요. 당신이 잘하면 상사의 일도 훨씬 수월해지거든요. 그래서 우리가 빠지기 쉬운 생각이 '아니야, 아니야, 저 사람들이 날 시험하는 거야'인데, 사실 그렇지 않아요.
text_zh: 没有人比你的经理更希望你表现出色了，因为你干得越好，你经理的日子就越好过。但我觉得咱们总是会钻牛角尖，老想着"不对不对，他们这是在考验我。"其实根本不是这么回事。
text_es: Nadie quiere que seas más exitoso que tu jefe, porque cuando rindes increíble, a tu jefe se le facilita todo, la vida se le hace más fácil. Entonces, creo que la mentalidad en la que caemos es como 'No, no, no. Me están probando.' Pero no es así.
key_sentence: Nobody wants you to be more awesome than your manager does, because when you're amazing, your manager, his life gets easier, her life gets easier.
original_text: Nobody wants you to be more awesome than your manager does, because when you're amazing, your manager, his life gets easier, her life gets easier. So, I just think that's the mentality we get into is like, 'No, no, no. They're testing me.' They're not. They are rooting for you.

vocabulary.definition: A mindset or way of thinking that influences behavior and attitudes.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, mentality often refers to the collective attitudes of a team or organization, which can significantly impact productivity and innovation.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'mentality' can imply a fixed way of thinking, it can also suggest the potential for change and growth in perspective.

vocabulary.definition: The process of evaluating or assessing something to determine its quality, performance, or reliability.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business or tech environment, testing is crucial for product development, ensuring that software or services meet required standards before launch.
vocabulary.nuance: Testing can carry a negative connotation when perceived as a challenge or obstacle, but it is fundamentally a necessary step for improvement and quality assurance.

text: We've turned that on its head, and it sounds great, but it's not free.
speaker: Andrew 'Boz' Bosworth
context: Lenny asks about Meta's culture of extreme transparency, where employees can ask executives questions directly and all data is shared openly. Boz explains that while most companies carefully curate what information employees receive, Meta gives access to almost everything and expects employees to filter it themselves. This creates tremendous empowerment but requires people to develop sophisticated systems for managing information overload and distinguishing important updates from irrelevant noise.
text_ko: 우린 그걸 완전히 뒤집어 놨어요. 듣기엔 정말 멋진데, 공짜로 되는 건 아니에요.
text_zh: 我们把这个完全颠倒过来了，听起来很不错，但这不是免费的。
text_es: Le dimos la vuelta a todo eso, y suena genial, pero no sale gratis.
key_sentence: it sounds great, but it's not free.
original_text: We've turned that on its head, and it sounds great, but it's not free. Even somebody senior coming from outside of the company to the company, one of the things I have to coach them on is, how do you find signal amongst all the noise?

text: Now News Feed was an easier case than people suspect, because everyone was outraged at the same time as they immediately doubled their usage of the product.
speaker: Andrew 'Boz' Bosworth
context: Lenny asks about building the Facebook News Feed, which was highly controversial when it launched but became essential to what people think of as Facebook today. Boz explains that while users were vocally angry about the new feature, their behavior told a different story - they were refreshing and using the product much more frequently. This created a clear signal that there was cognitive dissonance between what users said they wanted versus their revealed preferences through actual usage patterns.
text_ko: 뉴스 피드(News Feed)는 사람들이 생각하는 것보다 더 쉬운 사례였어요. 모두가 분노했지만 동시에 그 서비스를 즉시 두 배로 사용했거든요.
text_zh: 其实动态消息(News Feed)比大家想的要好处理，因为所有人一边骂得要死，一边使用频率直接翻了一倍。
text_es: Mira, el News Feed fue un caso más fácil de lo que la gente piensa, porque aunque todos estaban súper molestos, al mismo tiempo duplicaron el uso del producto de un día para otro.
key_sentence: News Feed was an easier case than people suspect; usage doubled during outrage.

vocabulary.definition: Feeling or showing strong displeasure or anger due to a perceived injustice or wrongdoing.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business settings, being outraged can refer to customer reactions to policies, product changes, or corporate decisions that are viewed as unfair or unethical.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'outraged' conveys a strong emotional response, it may be seen as overly dramatic in formal business communications; consider using 'concerned' in less intense situations.

vocabulary.definition: Increased twofold; to make or become twice as much or as many.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business context, 'doubled' often refers to metrics such as revenue, user engagement, or production output that have significantly increased, indicating growth or success.
vocabulary.nuance: The term 'doubled' implies a substantial increase and should be used when the growth is noteworthy; avoid it for minor increases.

vocabulary.definition: The manner in which something is used; the frequency or extent of use of a particular product or service.
vocabulary.businessContext: In tech and startup environments, 'usage' metrics are critical for understanding customer engagement, product performance, and areas for improvement.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'usage' is a neutral term, it can imply a need for analysis or optimization when discussing product performance; be cautious of its implications in competitive contexts.

text: When I reflect back on what really worked across my career, it really comes down to this: I just was willing to learn aggressively. I would move because I wasn't learning enough. I was bored, and so I wasn't learning enough new stuff.
speaker: Andrew 'Boz' Bosworth
context: Lenny asks about career advice, particularly regarding how much time to spend on different types of projects. Boz reflects on his unusual career path at Meta, where he changed roles every six months early on while his peers stayed in single tracks and got promoted faster initially. He explains that his willingness to keep moving to learn new things eventually paid off dramatically when he finally found roles deep enough to sustain his learning for years, leading to rapid vertical career growth.
text_ko: 돌아보면 제 커리어에서 진짜로 통했던 건 결국 이거였어요: 배우는 데 매우 적극적이었어요. 배울 게 충분하지 않다고 느끼면 자리를 옮겼고, 지루해지면 그건 곧 새로운 걸 충분히 배우지 못하고 있다는 신호였어요.
text_zh: 回头想想我职业生涯中真正有效的东西，其实就是这么回事：我特别愿意去学新东西，学得很猛。如果我觉得学不到什么了，我就会换地方。因为我会觉得无聊，学不到新玩意儿。
text_es: Cuando miro hacia atrás en lo que realmente funcionó en mi carrera, todo se reduce a esto: simplemente tenía las ganas de aprender a full. Me cambiaba de trabajo porque no estaba aprendiendo lo suficiente. Me aburría, y por eso no estaba aprendiendo cosas nuevas.
key_sentence: I was willing to learn aggressively because I wasn't learning enough new stuff.

vocabulary.definition: To think deeply or carefully about something, often in order to gain insight or understanding.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, reflecting on past experiences can help individuals and teams identify successful strategies and areas for improvement.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'reflect' suggests a thoughtful consideration, it can imply a more passive process compared to 'analyze' or 'evaluate'.

vocabulary.definition: In a manner that is assertive and forceful, often with a sense of urgency or intensity.
vocabulary.businessContext: Aggressively pursuing opportunities or strategies can indicate a proactive approach to market competition and growth.
vocabulary.nuance: The term can carry a positive connotation of determination but may also suggest a risk of being overly confrontational or pushy.

vocabulary.definition: Ready, eager, or prepared to do something, often implying a positive attitude towards taking action.
vocabulary.businessContext: A willing employee is often seen as an asset, as they are more likely to embrace new challenges and adapt to change.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'willing' suggests openness, it may lack the urgency or commitment implied by terms like 'eager' or 'enthusiastic'.

text: Communication is the job is, I really believe... whenever something goes wrong, I ask myself, 'What could I have done differently in terms of how I communicated things for this to have gone better?'
speaker: Andrew 'Boz' Bosworth
context: Lenny asks Boz to explain his famous post 'Communication is the Job.' Boz argues that if you want to have any impact on the world around you, it happens exclusively through communication - creating artifacts or verbalizations that affect other humans. He practices extreme ownership by always examining his own communication when things go wrong, rather than blaming others for misunderstanding or poor execution.
text_ko: 저는 소통 자체가 업무의 핵심이라고 정말 믿어요. 무언가 잘못될 때마다 스스로에게 "이 상황이 더 잘 풀리려면 내가 소통을 어떻게 달리했어야 했을까?"라고 물어봐요.
text_zh: 沟通就是工作本身，我是真的这么认为的...每当出什么问题的时候，我都会问自己，'在沟通方面，我要是换个方式说，事情会不会处理得更好？'
text_es: La comunicación es realmente el trabajo, yo creo firmemente que... cada vez que algo sale mal, me pregunto: '¿Qué pude haber hecho diferente en cuanto a cómo comuniqué las cosas para que esto hubiera salido mejor?'
key_sentence: what could I have done differently in terms of how I communicated things for this to have gone better?

vocabulary.definition: The act of conveying information, thoughts, or feelings to others through spoken, written, or non-verbal means.
vocabulary.businessContext: Effective communication is vital in business for ensuring clarity, alignment, and collaboration among teams and stakeholders.
vocabulary.nuance: The term can imply varying levels of effectiveness; thus, it is important to assess whether the communication was clear and understood.

vocabulary.definition: In a manner that is not the same as another; in an alternative way.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business context, considering how to approach a situation differently can lead to innovative solutions and improved outcomes.
vocabulary.nuance: The term suggests a need for reflection and adaptability, often implying that previous methods were inadequate.
